verses.pali: Aṅguttara Nikāya 3.99
verses.english: Numbered Discourses 3.99

verses.pali: 10. Loṇakapallavagga
verses.english: 10. A Lump of Salt

verses.pali: Potthakasutta
verses.english: Jute

verses.pali: “Navopi, bhikkhave, potthako dubbaṇṇo ca hoti dukkhasamphasso ca appaggho ca;
verses.english: “Jute canvas is ugly, unpleasant to touch, and worthless whether it’s new, worn in, or worn out.

verses.pali: majjhimopi, bhikkhave, potthako dubbaṇṇo ca hoti dukkhasamphasso ca appaggho ca;
jiṇṇopi, bhikkhave, potthako dubbaṇṇo ca hoti dukkhasamphasso ca appaggho ca.
Jiṇṇampi, bhikkhave, potthakaṁ ukkhaliparimajjanaṁ vā karonti saṅkārakūṭe vā naṁ chaḍḍenti.
verses.english: They use worn out jute canvas for scrubbing cauldrons, or else they just throw it away on the rubbish heap.

verses.pali: Evamevaṁ kho, bhikkhave, navo cepi bhikkhu hoti dussīlo pāpadhammo.
verses.english: In the same way, if a junior mendicant is unethical, of bad character,

verses.pali: Idamassa dubbaṇṇatāya vadāmi.
verses.english: this is how they’re ugly, I say.

verses.pali: Seyyathāpi so, bhikkhave, potthako dubbaṇṇo tathūpamāhaṁ, bhikkhave, imaṁ puggalaṁ vadāmi.
verses.english: That individual is just as ugly as jute canvas.

verses.pali: Ye kho panassa sevanti bhajanti payirupāsanti diṭṭhānugatiṁ āpajjanti, tesaṁ taṁ hoti dīgharattaṁ ahitāya dukkhāya.
verses.english: If you associate with, accompany, and attend to them, following their example, it’ll be for your lasting harm and suffering.

verses.pali: Idamassa dukkhasamphassatāya vadāmi.
verses.english: This is how they’re unpleasant to touch, I say.

verses.pali: Seyyathāpi so, bhikkhave, potthako dukkhasamphasso tathūpamāhaṁ, bhikkhave, imaṁ puggalaṁ vadāmi.
verses.english: That individual is just as unpleasant to touch as jute canvas.

verses.pali: Yesaṁ kho pana so paṭiggaṇhāti cīvarapiṇḍapātasenāsanagilānappaccayabhesajjaparikkhāraṁ, tesaṁ taṁ na mahapphalaṁ hoti na mahānisaṁsaṁ.
verses.english: Any robes, almsfood, lodgings, and medicines and supplies for the sick that they receive are not very fruitful or beneficial for the donor.

verses.pali: Idamassa appagghatāya vadāmi.
verses.english: This is how they’re worthless, I say.

verses.pali: Seyyathāpi so, bhikkhave, potthako appaggho tathūpamāhaṁ, bhikkhave, imaṁ puggalaṁ vadāmi.
verses.english: That individual is just as worthless as jute canvas.

verses.pali: Majjhimo cepi, bhikkhave, bhikkhu hoti …pe…
verses.english: If a middle mendicant is unethical, of bad character, this is how they’re ugly, I say. …

verses.pali: thero cepi, bhikkhave, bhikkhu hoti dussīlo pāpadhammo, idamassa dubbaṇṇatāya vadāmi.
verses.english: If a senior mendicant is unethical, of bad character, this is how they’re ugly, I say. …

verses.pali: Seyyathāpi so, bhikkhave, potthako dubbaṇṇo tathūpamāhaṁ, bhikkhave, imaṁ puggalaṁ vadāmi.
Ye kho panassa sevanti bhajanti payirupāsanti diṭṭhānugatiṁ āpajjanti, tesaṁ taṁ hoti dīgharattaṁ ahitāya dukkhāya.
verses.english: If you associate with, accompany, and attend to them, following their example, it’ll be for your lasting harm and suffering. …

verses.pali: Idamassa dukkhasamphassatāya vadāmi.
Seyyathāpi so, bhikkhave, potthako dukkhasamphasso tathūpamāhaṁ, bhikkhave, imaṁ puggalaṁ vadāmi.
Yesaṁ kho pana so paṭiggaṇhāti cīvarapiṇḍapātasenāsanagilānappaccayabhesajjaparikkhāraṁ, tesaṁ taṁ na mahapphalaṁ hoti na mahānisaṁsaṁ.
Idamassa appagghatāya vadāmi.
Seyyathāpi so, bhikkhave, potthako appaggho tathūpamāhaṁ, bhikkhave, imaṁ puggalaṁ vadāmi.
Evarūpo cāyaṁ, bhikkhave, thero bhikkhu saṅghamajjhe bhaṇati.
verses.english: If such a senior mendicant speaks among the Saṅgha,

verses.pali: Tamenaṁ bhikkhū evamāhaṁsu:
verses.english: the mendicants say:

verses.pali: ‘kiṁ nu kho tuyhaṁ bālassa abyattassa bhaṇitena,
verses.english: ‘What’s an incompetent fool like you got to say?

verses.pali: tvampi nāma bhaṇitabbaṁ maññasī’ti.
verses.english: How on earth could you imagine you’ve got something worth saying!’

verses.pali: So kupito anattamano tathārūpiṁ vācaṁ nicchāreti yathārūpāya vācāya saṅgho taṁ ukkhipati, saṅkārakūṭeva naṁ potthakaṁ.
verses.english: They become angry and upset, and blurt out things that make the Saṅgha throw them out, as if they were throwing jute canvas away on the rubbish heap.

verses.pali: Navampi, bhikkhave, kāsikaṁ vatthaṁ vaṇṇavantañceva hoti sukhasamphassañca mahagghañca; majjhimampi, bhikkhave, kāsikaṁ vatthaṁ vaṇṇavantañceva hoti sukhasamphassañca mahagghañca; jiṇṇampi, bhikkhave, kāsikaṁ vatthaṁ vaṇṇavantañceva hoti sukhasamphassañca mahagghañca.
verses.english: Cloth from Kāsi is beautiful, pleasant to touch, and valuable whether it’s new, worn in, or worn out.

verses.pali: Jiṇṇampi, bhikkhave, kāsikaṁ vatthaṁ ratanapaliveṭhanaṁ vā karoti gandhakaraṇḍake vā naṁ pakkhipanti.
verses.english: They use worn out cloth from Kāsi for wrapping, or else they place it in a fragrant casket.

verses.pali: Evamevaṁ kho, bhikkhave, navo cepi bhikkhu hoti sīlavā kalyāṇadhammo, idamassa suvaṇṇatāya vadāmi.
verses.english: In the same way, if a junior mendicant is ethical, of good character, this is how they’re beautiful, I say.

verses.pali: Seyyathāpi taṁ, bhikkhave, kāsikaṁ vatthaṁ vaṇṇavantaṁ tathūpamāhaṁ, bhikkhave, imaṁ puggalaṁ vadāmi.
verses.english: That individual is just as beautiful as cloth from Kāsi.

verses.pali: Ye kho panassa sevanti bhajanti payirupāsanti diṭṭhānugatiṁ āpajjanti, tesaṁ taṁ hoti dīgharattaṁ hitāya sukhāya.
verses.english: If you associate with, accompany, and attend to such an individual, following their example, it will be for your lasting welfare and happiness.

verses.pali: Idamassa sukhasamphassatāya vadāmi.
verses.english: This is how they’re pleasant to touch, I say.

verses.pali: Seyyathāpi taṁ, bhikkhave, kāsikaṁ vatthaṁ sukhasamphassaṁ tathūpamāhaṁ, bhikkhave, imaṁ puggalaṁ vadāmi.
verses.english: That individual is just as pleasant to touch as cloth from Kāsi.

verses.pali: Yesaṁ kho pana so paṭiggaṇhāti cīvarapiṇḍapātasenāsanagilānappaccayabhesajjaparikkhāraṁ, tesaṁ taṁ mahapphalaṁ hoti mahānisaṁsaṁ.
verses.english: Any robes, almsfood, lodgings, and medicines and supplies for the sick that they receive are very fruitful and beneficial for the donor.

verses.pali: Idamassa mahagghatāya vadāmi.
verses.english: This is how they’re valuable, I say.

verses.pali: Seyyathāpi taṁ, bhikkhave, kāsikaṁ vatthaṁ mahagghaṁ tathūpamāhaṁ, bhikkhave, imaṁ puggalaṁ vadāmi.
verses.english: That individual is just as valuable as cloth from Kāsi.

verses.pali: Majjhimo cepi, bhikkhave, bhikkhu hoti …pe…
verses.english: If a middle mendicant is ethical, of good character, this is how they’re beautiful, I say. …

verses.pali: thero cepi, bhikkhave, bhikkhu hoti …pe… puggalaṁ vadāmi.
verses.english: If a senior mendicant is ethical, of good character, this is how they’re beautiful, I say. …

verses.pali: Evarūpo cāyaṁ, bhikkhave, thero bhikkhu saṅghamajjhe bhaṇati.
verses.english: If such a senior mendicant speaks in the midst of the Saṅgha,

verses.pali: Tamenaṁ bhikkhū evamāhaṁsu:
verses.english: the mendicants say:

verses.pali: ‘appasaddā āyasmanto hotha, thero bhikkhu dhammañca vinayañca bhaṇatī’ti.
verses.english: ‘Venerables, be quiet! The senior mendicant is speaking on the teaching and training.’

verses.pali: Tasmātiha, bhikkhave, evaṁ sikkhitabbaṁ:
verses.english: So you should train like this:

verses.pali: ‘kāsikavatthūpamā bhavissāma, na potthakūpamā’ti.
verses.english: ‘We will be like cloth from Kāsi, not like jute canvas.’

verses.pali: Evañhi vo, bhikkhave, sikkhitabban”ti.
verses.english: That’s how you should train.”

verses.pali: Aṭṭhamaṁ.
